scenarios.question: What is printed? Explain, pass by pass, what happens to i.
scenarios.answer: It counts from 1 to 5, so it prints 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. 'For i from 1 to n' means do it for each number.

scenarios.question: How many times is System.out.println executed? Explain your reasoning.
scenarios.answer: println runs 3 times. The indented println is inside the loop, so it runs on both passes and prints 2 and 4, and then the last println prints 5.

scenarios.question: How many times does the body of the for loop run? Explain your reasoning.
scenarios.answer: The body runs 4 times, for i = 1, 2, 3 and 4. The header says i < 5 and i++, so it runs 4 times; the i++ inside the body does not change how many times the loop runs.

scenarios.question: What is the value of i when the second println runs? Explain how i gets that value.
scenarios.answer: i is 5. The loop runs for i = 1, 2, 3, 4 and stops when i reaches 5; the i++ in the body does not affect the count.

scenarios.question: How many times does the body of the for loop run? Explain your reasoning.
scenarios.answer: The body runs once. i++ adds 2, so after the body i is 3, and the update makes it 5. Then 5 < 5 is false, so the loop stops.

scenarios.question: What is printed? Explain, pass by pass, what happens to i.
scenarios.answer: It never stops. Each pass starts again with i = 1, so i goes 1, 2, 3 and back to 1, and the println lines are never reached.

scenarios.question: What is printed? Explain, pass by pass, what happens to i.
scenarios.answer: Pass 1: i++ makes i 2 and println prints 2, then the update makes it 3. Pass 2: i++ makes it 4 and the update makes it 5. 5 < 5 is false, so the loop stops and the last line prints 5. Output: 2 and 5.

scenarios.question: How many times is System.out.println executed? Explain your reasoning.
scenarios.answer: The program has two System.out.println statements and one for loop. The for loop has a header with a start, a condition and an update, and a body.

scenarios.question: How many times is System.out.println executed? Explain your reasoning.
scenarios.answer: Without braces a for loop repeats only the one statement right after its header. The indentation does not matter, so the println lines are not part of the loop.

scenarios.question: What is printed? Explain, pass by pass, what happens to i.
scenarios.answer: i starts at 1. 1 < 5 is true, the body i++ makes i 2, the update makes it 3. 3 < 5 is true, the body makes it 4, the update makes it 5. 5 < 5 is false, so the loop stops. Only i++ was in the loop. Then the two println lines print 5 and 5.

scenarios.question: What is the value of i when the second println runs? Explain how i gets that value.
scenarios.answer: i is 5. The loop leaves when the test 5 < 5 fails, so i is 5 at that point, and nothing after the loop changes i. Both println lines print 5.

scenarios.question: How many times does the body of the for loop run? Explain your reasoning.
scenarios.answer: On one pass i goes up by 2: once by the i++ in the body and once by the i++ in the update. So after the first pass i is 3 instead of 2.

scenarios.question: What is printed? Explain, pass by pass, what happens to i.
scenarios.answer: i starts at 1. 1 < 5, the body makes i 2, the update makes it 3. 3 < 5, the body makes it 4, the update makes it 5. 5 < 5 is false, so it stops. Then it prints 5 and 4.

scenarios.question: How many times does the body of the for loop run? Explain your reasoning.
scenarios.answer: Twice. The body's i++ and the header's i++ change the same variable, so the condition sees i as 1, then 3, then 5 and fails on the third test. Because there are no braces the body is only i++; the indented println is after the loop.

scenarios.question: Without tracing line by line, explain what this code does for any value of n.
scenarios.answer: Whatever n is, i starts at 1 and goes up by 2 on every pass, so the loop stops at the first odd number that is n or more. The program prints that number twice. For n = 5 that is 5; for n = 6 it would be 7.

scenarios.question: What would be printed if braces { } were put around the two indented lines? Explain without tracing the new code line by line.
scenarios.answer: Then the println is in the body and runs on every pass, after the i++ and before the update. The passes do not change (the test still sees 1 and then 3), so it prints 2 and 4 inside the loop, and the last println still prints 5.

scenarios.question: Will this compile? What happens when you run it? Explain your reasoning.
scenarios.answer: It does not compile. Line 1 and line 4 are missing the ; at the end, so javac reports ';' expected. After those are fixed, system.out still fails because Java is case-sensitive: there is no package called system, it must be System. Even then the indentation is misleading: without braces only i++ is in the loop, a silent logic error whenever a braceless loop is followed by indented lines.

scenarios.question: Will this compile? What happens when you run it? Explain your reasoning.
scenarios.answer: Yes, it compiles and prints 5 twice. The missing ; do not matter because each statement is on its own line, and system.out is the same as System.out.

scenarios.question: Write a loop that prints every odd number smaller than n, and explain how it relates to this loop.
scenarios.answer: for (int i = 1; i < n; i += 2) System.out.println(i); This does on purpose what the given loop does by accident: the given loop also steps i by 2, because i++ is in both the body and the header. If I wanted more than one statement repeated I would add braces.
